title: Classical clarinet studies at Jersey City State
summary: Studying with David Dworkin and Herbert Blayman of the Met Opera orchestra, who gave him jazz-oriented repertoire.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: What was your classical training on the clarinet?

I studied with David Dworkin, who was a clarinetist with the Metropolitan Opera Orchestra. And it was the same situation, I was studying in college, I went to Jersey City State, which is a music college in Jersey City, New Jersey. That’s where I grew up was New Jersey. So I studied with him and I studied some with Herbert Blamin who was the principal clarinetist with the opera orchestra, the Metropolitan Opera Orchestra. But both

of them were well aware that I was not interested in becoming a symphonic player or anything, so I would play things that were more jazz oriented — works like Ravel or Alec Wilder or composers like that. That’s what they would have me do because they would tell me, you’re not going to be a classical musician, what’s the point of learning the standard repertoire. If you want to learn to just play the instrument we’re here to teach you how to play the instrument better so you can do the things that you want. They were both very good teachers. And at the same time that’s when I was studying with Kenny.
